lessons.title: What is a presentation?
outcomes: Identify the main types of presentation you may be asked to give.
Describe where presenting is used beyond assessment.

lessons.title: Reading the brief
outcomes: Identify what a presentation brief asks you to do.
Distinguish what a brief requires from what it leaves to you.

lessons.title: Research and planning
outcomes: Describe the steps between receiving a brief and having a workable plan.
Recognise what makes a plan usable.

lessons.title: Designing visual aids
outcomes: Distinguish a visual aid that carries a point from one that carries a script.
Recognise features that make a slide or poster support the speaker.

lessons.title: Structuring your argument
outcomes: Explain how a conclusion that returns to the objectives closes the argument.

decidedValue.note: 5 lessons. Step 5 of the recipe (practise) is named in L06's practical-guidance block only; full delivery treatment is Intermediate. Rationale for five over four: the four-lesson shape merged research/planning with visual aids; splitting them was chosen deliberately with the thin-lesson risk accepted and mitigated by requiring a full worked example in each. Interior patterns and check-component choices per lesson are DEFERRED to Phase B. Thin-lesson risk on L04/L05 logged to backlog 5.59.

alternativesConsidered.whyNot: Contradicts CTX's closed subject facet (psychology): the record would say the course is for psychology students while building with the generic pack. DL-1 AMENDMENT establishes the facet states who the instance is for, not merely an unconsumed label; the fact that nothing yet reads it mechanically changes what enforces the coupling, not what the design record should say.

Archive's build closed no subject facet at CTX, so a multi-pack spread was the only way to serve more than one discipline. This build closes a single psychology subject facet at CTX, so a single matching pack is the more precise fit; no grounding supplies a reason to widen beyond it.

confidenceItems: I can name the main types of presentation and say where each one is used.
I can work out what a presentation brief is asking me to do, and what it leaves to me.
I can get from a brief to a workable plan for a presentation.
I can tell the difference between a slide that supports what I'm saying and one that just repeats it.
I can structure a presentation so it opens with a hook and closes by returning to the objectives.
decidedValue.note: Five items, one per lesson, each folding that lesson's two A3 outcomes into a single ratable first-person claim. Deliberately coarser than the outcomes themselves. Group id: presenting-introductory-confidence.
